sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the number of persons who check in for at least a night at a tourist centre. (b) International tourist ________ are expenditures made by inbound visitors.
questions.answer: (a) Tourist arrivals. (b) Receipts.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Tourist arrivals means the number of persons who get accommodation at a tourist centre for at least 48 hours. (b) In 2012, America recorded the highest growth in total international tourist arrivals.
questions.answer: (a) False: for at least a night. (b) False: Asia and the Pacific recorded the highest growth (7%).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) UNWTO stands for ________. (b) According to the UNWTO Annual Report of 2015, the country that gets the highest number of tourists in the world is ________.
questions.answer: (a) United Nations World Tourism Organization. (b) France.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The World Tourism Day is celebrated on ________. (b) The number of international tourists who visited Africa in 2015 was ________ million.
questions.answer: (a) 27 September. (b) 53.

questions.q: True or False. (a) The trend of international tourist arrivals is almost continuously on the rise. (b) Europe and America held only 50% of arrivals in 1950.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: they held about 95%.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The world tourist arrivals in 2015 were ________ million. (b) The growth rate of world tourism is on average about ________ per cent a year.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Olympics (b) Casinos. B: (i) Entertainment attraction (ii) Mega sports event (iii) Natural attraction.
True or False. (a) Tourism is more concentrated in developed countries of Europe and North America. (b) The share of South Asia in world tourism is very high.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it is very low.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The single largest source of tourists today is the ________ class of developing countries. (b) The UNWTO headquarters are in ________ (Spain).
questions.answer: (a) Middle (growing middle class). (b) Madrid.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: 'The trend of international tourist arrivals is almost continuously on the rise.' Support the statement with two relevant arguments.
questions.answer: World arrivals rose from 530 million in 1995 to 1,035 million in 2012 and 1,184 million in 2015. Arrivals grew every year since 2010 by about 4% or more, with only a small dip around 2003.

questions.q: 'Package providers are of great help to the tourists.' Analyse the statement in two points.
questions.answer: They prepare the itinerary as per the tourists' demand and make a hassle-free tour. Where tour operators work, tourism is more prominent on the world tourist map.

questions.q: Mention any two attractions for tourists at destinations in the world.
questions.answer: Cultural attractions such as historical sites, monuments and museums. Natural attractions such as landscapes, beaches, mountains and parks, and events such as festivals and sports.

questions.q: Differentiate between natural landscapes and cultural landscapes in two points.
questions.answer: Natural landscapes (mountains, beaches, parks) are created by nature and are attractive for scenery. Cultural landscapes (monuments, museums, architecture, festivals) are created by people and show history and culture.

questions.q: How does travel cost affect tourism in the world?
questions.answer: Moderate to low cost boosts tourism while high cost is a hindrance. It matters less for very rich people.

questions.q: Describe the growth of world tourism since 2011.
questions.answer: Arrivals were 983 million in 2011, 1,087 million in 2013 and 1,184 million in 2015, with growth of about 4% every year.

questions.q: What is meant by sports tourism?
questions.answer: It is the movement of tourists to take part in or watch sports elsewhere, such as golf, tennis, cricket, snow sports and world cups.

questions.q: Name any three of the top ten tourist destinations of the world in 2015.
questions.answer: France, the United States and Spain (then Italy, the United Kingdom, China, Poland, Mexico, Canada and Hungary).

questions.q: Why has the share of Europe and the Americas in world tourism declined?
questions.answer: New destinations in East Asia, the Pacific, the Middle East and other developing regions have grown. These regions grow faster, reducing the share of Europe and America.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three attractions for the tourists at destinations in the world.
questions.answer: (i) Cultural: historical and archaeological sites, monuments, museums and cuisine. (ii) Natural: landscapes, mountains, beaches, islands, parks, flora and fauna. (iii) Events and recreation: festivals, the Olympics, trade fairs, sightseeing, golf, snow sports and amusement parks.

questions.q: Explain the factors affecting world tourism in three points (any three).
questions.answer: (i) High income and paid holidays give people money and time to travel. (ii) Low travel cost and technology (internet information) encourage travel. (iii) Package providers, media and the growing middle class of developing countries boost tourism.

questions.q: Explain the spatial distribution of world tourism in three points.
questions.answer: (i) It depends on natural landscape, beautiful sites, accessibility and moderate climate. (ii) Man-made beautification, monuments, gardens and religious festivals also attract tourists. (iii) It is concentrated in Europe, the Mediterranean and the USA but is growing in developing countries.

questions.q: Explain the share of the world regions in international tourist arrivals in 2015 (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Europe had the highest share, 609 million (51%). (ii) Asia and the Pacific followed with 278 million (23%), then the Americas with 191 million. (iii) Africa had the minimum, 53 million (5%), and the Middle East 54 million.

questions.q: Explain the future prospects of world tourism (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Arrivals are expected to grow about 4% a year. (ii) Europe will remain the top destination (about 717 million by 2020) and East Asia and the Pacific will grow 6.5% a year. (iii) Africa, the Middle East and South Asia will grow quickly from a low base.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any six factors affecting tourism in the world.
questions.answer: (i) High income and per capita income of tourists. (ii) Paid holidays or holiday entitlement. (iii) Travel cost: low to moderate costs boost tourism. (iv) Technology: information on the internet. (v) Package providers and tour operators make touring easy, and print and audio-visual media create awareness. (vi) A growing middle class in developing countries and new destinations with tourism investment.

questions.q: Explain the growth and pattern of world tourism in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Tourism flourished from the mid-20th century. (ii) Europe and America had 95% of arrivals in 1950 but 76% by 2000. (iii) East Asia and the Pacific grew about 13% a year and the Middle East 10%. (iv) Arrivals rose from 983 million (2011) to 1,184 million (2015). (v) Europe takes 51% of arrivals and 41% of receipts. (vi) Receipts were US$ 1,245 billion in 2014 and arrivals are expected to grow about 4% a year.

questions.q: Describe the attractions for tourists at destinations in the world, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Cultural attractions: historical and archaeological sites, monuments and museums. (ii) Natural attractions: landscapes, seascapes, mountains, beaches, flora and fauna. (iii) Events: mega-events, trade fairs, conferences and community festivals. (iv) Religious events such as the Haj and Maha Kumbh. (v) Sports events such as the Olympics and world cups, and recreation like golf and snow sports. (vi) Entertainment such as theme parks, casinos and shopping.
